story_text:
## Print it. Build it. Let it spell.
Build your own compact, 3D-printed Spirit Board with a moving pointer and a phone interface. Ask a question in AI mode, or choose the words yourself in Manual Mode—and watch the board spell them out.
I designed this project to combine a mysterious atmosphere with an accessible DIY build. Its compact size and simple mechanism are central to the design: a small tabletop project you can print, assemble, and bring to life yourself.
## Two ways to use your board
In AI Séance mode, ask a question through the phone interface and let an AI-generated response guide the moving pointer.
In Manual Mode, you control the message. Send your own text or select YES or NO directly from your phone.
Your phone and the board must be connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
The interface follows the board’s dark and gold design, bringing the physical object and its controls together into one experience.
## What you receive
This campaign offers a digital DIY build package, including:
- STL files for the printable parts.
- Source code for the board and its phone interface.
- A complete components list (about $50 in parts, depending on suppliers).
- Assembly and wiring instructions.
The board is 21 cm wide. Printing the complete set takes approximately 10 hours, depending on your printer and print settings, and requires around 300 g of filament.
You print the parts and purchase the electronics separately. Assembly requires soldering skills, basic wiring knowledge, and familiarity with uploading firmware using tools such as the Arduino IDE. You will need a suitable 3D printer, soldering tools, and a computer for the initial setup.
We aim to release the complete project files by October 24, 2026 — one week before Halloween.
The hardware list will be shared in a backer-only Kickstarter update around October 16, 2026, so you can order the components in advance.
You’ll receive an email with a download link as soon as the files are ready. Printing takes approximately 10 hours, depending on your printer and settings. After printing, assembly, soldering, and firmware setup should take around one evening for someone familiar with these tasks.
AI mode requires an internet connection and an external AI service. Any applicable AI service charges are separate from the project files.
If you enjoy 3D printing, interactive props, or unusual electronics projects, this is an invitation to build something with a little more atmosphere.
Print the pieces. Assemble the mechanism. Start your séance.
risks: Print quality and mechanical fit can vary between printers, materials, and settings. Builders may need to adjust print settings or perform minor fitting and calibration. I will provide recommended settings and assembly guidance to help with this process. Electronic component availability and prices may vary by country. The documentation will identify the required components and specifications. AI mode depends on an external AI service and an internet connection. Service availability, pricing, and compatibility may change, and AI responses can be unpredictable. Any applicable service fees are the builder’s responsibility. Manual Mode works independently of the AI service and does not require an internet connection. The delivery schedule may change if preparing the files or documentation takes longer than expected. I will keep backers informed of progress, any issues, and revised delivery estimates. This campaign provides digital files and instructions. Backers are responsible for printing the parts, obtaining the components and tools, and assembling their own board. No physical board, printed parts, or electronics are included.

faq.q: Am I receiving a physical board?
faq.a: No. This is a digital DIY project. You receive the files and instructions needed to print and assemble your own board. Physical parts, electronics, and tools are not included.

faq.q: What is included in the digital package?
faq.a: STL files, source code for the board and its phone interface, a complete components list, and assembly and wiring instructions.

faq.q: How big is the board, and how much printing is required?
faq.a: The board is 21 cm wide. The complete set requires approximately 300 g of filament and around 10 hours of printing, depending on your printer and settings.

faq.q: What skills and tools do I need?
faq.a: You need soldering skills, basic wiring knowledge, and familiarity with uploading firmware using tools such as the Arduino IDE. You will also need a suitable 3D printer, soldering tools, and a computer for setup.

faq.q: How much do the additional components cost?
faq.a: Budget approximately $50 USD for the required components, depending on suppliers and your location. Filament, tools, shipping, and any AI service fees are additional.

faq.q: How do I control the board?
faq.a: You control it through a web interface in your phone’s browser. Use AI Séance mode to ask questions, or Manual Mode to send your own text.

faq.q: Does the board require an internet connection?
faq.a: Manual Mode works without internet access or AI. AI Séance mode requires an internet connection and an external AI service. Any applicable AI service fees are separate from your pledge.

faq.q: When and how will I receive the files?
faq.a:
We aim to deliver the complete files by October 24, 2026. You’ll receive an email with a download link. 
The hardware list will be shared in a backer-only Kickstarter update around October 16, 2026, so you can order the components in advance.

faq.q: Can I build my board before Halloween?
faq.a: That’s the plan! If the files arrive as scheduled and you have your components ready, allow approximately 10 hours for printing and one evening for assembly and setup. Timing depends on your printer settings and experience, so please allow some extra time.

faq.q: Can I sell boards I make using these files?
faq.a: The Personal License is for non-commercial use. The Commercial License allows you to sell physical boards you produce. It does not permit reselling or sharing the STL files or the project’s source code.
